transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (AtlasMed Head of Search), Ethan Lee (AtlasMed ML Engineer), Priya Singh (AtlasMed CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick sales demo focusing on embeddings + rerank for product search relevance. Covered API flow, demo of vectors+reranking logic, simple benchmark numbers, and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we got about 40 minutes scheduled, i'll do a 5 minute intro and then jonah will dive into the demo and we'll leave time for q&a, sound good?
[00:18] Maya: sounds good, thanks Samira. we're excited - we just want to see a realistic embed + rerank flow for our product search.
[00:24] Priya: yes, quick note on timeline: we need something in pilot with infra approvals by the end of this month if possible.
[00:32] Samira: totally, that's helpful. quick intros - i'm samira, i'm the AE, and jonah's our solutions engineer who will show the API and the console. jonah?
[00:40] Jonah: yeah hi all, uh thanks. i'll start with the hosted api architecture for embeddings + rerank and then demo a small example with your sample dataset folder - caveat: i'll be using a demo dataset not your prod logs. (little laugh)
[00:55] Ethan: ok, FYI our stack today is an elastic search cluster for indexing + a simple dot-product reranker using faiss in a sidecar.
[01:03] Maya: and the pain points: cold start latency, cost of storing vectors, and relevance drift when new products are added.
[01:10] Jonah: super helpful. so high level - Redwood hosted provides embeddings endpoint and a rerank endpoint. typical flow: index vector embeddings (we have incremental indexing), at query time you do a dense retrieval top-k and then call rerank with the original query + candidate docs to get final reorder. the rerank endpoint uses a cross-encoder approach so it's higher quality than raw vector dot product.
[01:36] (small crosstalk)
[01:40] Maya: can you show latency numbers? how much slower is rerank than a simple dot product?
[01:45] Jonah: sure - in our notes, typical rerank cross-encoder latency is 60-120ms per request at 8-16 candidates on our hosted service for the medium-size model we use in demos. dot-product retrieval is sub-10ms from index. so you see the tradeoff. we also support streaming and chunked rerank for long documents.
[02:05] Ethan: 60-120ms - that's okay but on our mobile endpoints we want p95 under 200ms including network. how does batching help?
[02:12] Jonah: batching helps when you have many concurrent requests; Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and can amortize transformer cost - in hosted mode we can trade a small extra tail latency for much lower token cost. you can also set a max-latency SLO and we respect it.
[02:28] Priya: and for compliance we need SOC2 + ability to use our keys, is that possible?
[02:33] Samira: yes, we support SOC 2, we have audit logs and we offer KMS integration for Dedicated and in Private deployments. in hosted we can integrate with customer-managed keys for some customers - we'll share the security docs.
[02:45] Maya: ok good. uh how is data retention handled on hosted?
[02:49] Jonah: by default short retention but we can disable retention for specific endpoints and we provide per-tenant isolation. we'll send the retention policy doc.
[02:56] (pause)
[03:10] Jonah: demo time - i have a quick curl and python notebook. first step: create embedding for product descriptions, store in your vector index (we integrate with Pinecone, Faiss, and native Redwood vector store). then at query time call /v1/rerank with payload {query, candidates: [ids + embeddings or text]}. the API returns scores and a re-ranked list.
[03:35] Maya: are candidates passed as precomputed embeddings or raw text?
[03:38] Jonah: both. if you pass embeddings you save compute; if you pass raw text we compute them at rerank time which can increase latency. many customers compute embeddings at index time then pass ids + embeddings.
[03:51] Ethan: can you demo an example where we send top-10 from elastic then call rerank?
[03:55] Jonah: absolutely, i'll show a simulated flow.

[04:10] [DEMO START] Jonah: so i'm running a sample query "insulin pump mobile" - first i fetch top-12 by vector similarity from the index (simulated here). now i'll call the rerank endpoint with the query and candidate texts. curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"query":"insulin pump mobile","candidates":[{"id":"p1","text":"..."},...],"model":"rerank-medium"}'
[04:45] (keyboard typing noises)
[04:50] Jonah: response comes back with scores and new order - you can see the cross-encoder properly bumps product p7 that mentions "FDA-approved" higher than other matches that had similar vector prox.
[05:05] Maya: nice - that kind of nuance is exactly what we need.
[05:09] Jonah: also, we have a rerank scoring explainability field - it gives token-level attention importance, but it's an estimate (approx), useful for debugging relevance regressions.
[05:22] Ethan: how about throughput? if we have 200 qps across our search endpoints, can hosted handle that?
[05:29] Jonah: for hosted, we commonly carve multi-tenant pools. 200 qps rerank at 10 candidates is non-trivial; if you need predictable throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or we can set a higher SLA in hosted with throughput commitments. for pilots we usually start small - 50-100 qps simulated - and then move to dedicated if steady high qps.
[05:52] Priya: cost ballpark - what's the unit cost for embedding storage and rerank calls?
[05:58] Samira: i'll share the price sheet but rough numbers: embeddings store cost is per-vector-month small; the dominant cost is rerank compute per call (approximated per 1000 calls). we'll send a tailored estimate for your traffic shape.
[06:10] (brief pause)
[06:20] Maya: security follow-up - do you provide audit logs for inference requests? we need to show request-level logs for SOC 2 audit.
[06:27] Jonah: yes, hosted exposes audit logs with request metadata; for full content logging we can toggle redaction. We keep per-tenant logs for 90 days by default and longer with addons.
[06:39] Ethan: for our PII concerns, can we enable on-the-fly PII stripping?
[06:43] Jonah: we have pre-processing hooks and tokenizer-level filters; we can also recommend patterns to do PII removal before sending queries.
[06:50] Maya: ok good.

[07:05] [Benchmark talk] Jonah: quick numbers from our internal benchmark: using rerank-medium model, avg latency 85ms for 8 candidates with p95 140ms on hosted EU cluster. cost was about $X per 1000 rerank calls in that configuration (X will be in the pricing sheet).
[07:30] Maya: is model selection flexible? can we change model sizes for quality/cost?
[07:34] Jonah: yes, we have multiple rerank models and embedding models. you can pick a smaller model to save cost, or quantize in Dedicated. Redwood Optimize provides model recommendations based on your eval set.

[07:48] Ethan: do you support A/B rollouts of rerank models? we want to test new ranking without full cutover.
[07:53] Jonah: yep - console supports route-level rollouts, canary and percentage traffic splits, and automatic fallback rules if latency spikes.
[08:03] (customer mutters)

[08:20] Maya: question on integration effort - our infra team is small, how long does a pilot take?
[08:26] Samira: typical pilot 2-4 weeks: onboarding, a small traffic mirror or synthetic runner, run benchmarks, and review metrics. with your timeline we'll aim for 2 weeks if you can provide sample logs and a single test index.
[08:39] Priya: can Redwood do the initial index migration?
[08:42] Samira: yes, we can provide onboarding support - low-touch options or full-assisted migration for enterprise. we'll include those options in the pilot proposal.

[09:00] [Transcription hiccup] Speaker 1: um the - the reorg for the product match yeah
[09:07] Jonah: (laughs) that's okay.

[09:20] [Security deep-dive quick Q] Ethan: for KMS - if we bring our own key, can hosted still decrypt for processing? how does that work?
[09:28] Jonah: hosted with BYOK is possible for selected customers: keys are used to encrypt at-rest and we have secure enclaves for processing; some very sensitive customers opt for Dedicated or Private if they require full key control. we'll share the security whitepaper.

[09:45] Maya: do you have any compliance customers in healthcare?
[09:49] Samira: yes, we have a couple of medtech and health analytics customers on Dedicated and Private. we can share references under NDA.

[10:02] [Demo continued] Jonah: now i'll show the console: per-route dashboards show token-level cost, latency histograms, rerank score distributions, and an evaluation tab where you can upload prompts and expected relevance to run quality regression checks.
[10:20] (screen share noises)
[10:30] Jonah: here you can create an eval set, run it across models, and Redwood Optimize will suggest a model + quantization profile to meet a cost/quality target.
[10:40] Maya: can we plug our current eval suite into Optimize?
[10:43] Jonah: yes - you can upload CSV of queries + labels or use the API to submit evaluation runs.

[11:00] [Customer questions about data residency] Priya: our legal needs data to reside within EU regions for some customers. hosted supports region pinning?
[11:09] Jonah: yes, region pinning is supported; we can ensure inference and storage in EU regions. for stronger guarantees, Private deployment is available.

[11:25] Ethan: let's talk failure modes - if rerank backend is slow, do you fall back to vector-only scoring?
[11:31] Jonah: yes, we support automatic fallback policies: fallback to vector-sim, or to a smaller model, or to cached results. these are configurable per-route.

[11:45] Maya: good. okay any questions from us?
[11:48] Priya: timeline - if pilot starts next week, what are the blocking items?
[11:53] Samira: blockers: infra whitelisting of Redwood IPs, sample logs, and agreement on pilot SLOs. once those are done, onboarding takes 2-3 days, then tests.

[12:06] Ethan: we can provide sample logs by Monday and whitelist ip ranges, that's doable.
[12:12] Maya: regarding success metrics we want: 10% lift in top-3 click-through and p95 end-to-end latency under 200ms.
[12:20] Samira: perfect - we'll encode those as pilot success criteria.

[12:35] [Wrap-up] Samira: quick recap - action items: i will send pilot pricing and contract, jonah will share demo snippets and benchmark notes, ethan will share sample queries and top-10 logs. proposed pilot kickoff 2027-04-28, is that right?
[12:50] Maya: yes that works.
[12:53] Priya: yep.
[12:55] Samira: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links to security docs, the sample notebook, and the pricing sheet.
[13:05] (call ends)

Notes: transcript includes minor ASR errors: speaker labels occasionally generic, minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., "reorg" vs "re-rank"), occasional filler words. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-embeddings, redwood-benchmarks.csv (internal link), pilot-proposal.docx (will be attached).
